sentence: This project studies how cancer cells that survive therapy stay alive, focusing on cell death regulation and DNA repair.
This project offers tools for genetic screens and compound testing, including CRISPR and RNAi, to help study cancer.
This project studies how the heart changes differently by sex during myocardial fibrosis, using bioengineered models of disease.
This project studies how Notch signaling works in the pancreatic tumor microenvironment and how it affects T cells.
This project tests whether DNA methylation markers in blood can be used to detect pancreatic cancer early without invasive tests.
This project studies how RNA-guided systems that insert DNA and control genes work at a molecular level.
This project tracks how the material around ovarian cancer cells changes over time after chemotherapy, using tissue engineering and metabolic labeling.
This project tests a therapy that redirects a patient's own immune T cells against epithelial ovarian cancer.
This project studies nanoparticles that activate the innate immune system, aiming at immunotherapy against solid cancer.
This project studies how arrestin-1 binds rhodopsin in rod photoreceptors, using binding assays and recordings in mice.
This project studies how Barrett's esophagus turns into dysplasia, using single-cell RNA sequencing and 3D epithelial culture systems.
This project studies how HIV and opioids together affect mitochondria, inflammasome activation and neurotoxicity in human brain specimens.
This project studies how a modification on histone in endothelial cells under disturbed blood flow leads to atherosclerosis, using cell cultures and mouse models.
This project builds tools to improve value sets, which are lists of codes and terms that define clinical concepts.
This project builds a machine learning simulation that designs 3D-printed exoskeleton prototypes for each person to help older adults walk.
This project uses molecular imaging to study how a receptor differs between tumor lesions and whether that predicts response to antibody-drug conjugates.
This project builds a computer system that uses retinal imaging genetics data to predict ocular disease early and find patients at risk.
This project develops a rapid test that identifies microbes directly from infected blood and urine samples using lipidomic profiling.
This project studies how dopamine changes the activity of neurons, synapses and circuits to modify behavior.
This project studies how tau affects microtubule and mitochondrial dynamics and alveolar epithelial repair in the lung.
